goal: Find me good automation testers for this opening.

requirements.title: Automation Test Engineer
ambiguities: Does the role include API, mobile, or performance test automation, or is it web UI only? The JD names none of these, and HR only specified Selenium with Java.
Is the engineer expected to build or own a test automation framework, or to write and maintain tests inside an existing one?
Which certifications (e.g. ISTQB) or which domains (e.g. finance, healthcare) count as a plus?
Which CI/CD, test management, or BDD tools (e.g. Jenkins, TestNG, Cucumber) are expected under 'modern tools and practices'?
How much flexible-hours availability is expected (e.g. time-zone overlap with clients, on-call or evening calls)?

reply:
I screened 50 CVs against Selenium + Java (must-have), at least 3 years, web testing, and English required. 8 are ranked, 15 not shortlisted and 27 knocked out. None of the knock-outs looked like parse failures, and there were no near-ties. I reviewed the top 5 in detail, and the evidence quotes were checked against each CV.

Shortlist, best first:
1. CV-033: Built and maintains a Selenium + Java + TestNG framework (POM, data-driven tests, parallel Selenium Grid on Docker). Also has RestAssured API tests, GitLab CI checks, ISTQB, and mentors juniors. No explicit client-facing English, only a mixed Vietnamese/English team.
2. CV-039: Highest depth (L4). Built a shared automation platform adopted by 12 of 14 teams, with CI quality gates, Pact contract testing and Kubernetes runners. Covers Selenium/TestNG and Playwright, with outsourcing and financial-domain experience. No explicit client-facing English.
3. CV-038: L4 depth. Java/RestAssured framework used by several squads, merge-blocking CI gates, and daily English use with offshore teams. Caveat: the Selenium + Java work is brief and dated (2016–2017), and recent work is API and contract testing. Please check this against your Selenium must-have.
4. CV-027: Concrete Selenium + Java + TestNG: 180 scripts in an existing POM framework, Jenkins runs on a containerised Grid. English with US clients (sprint reviews, daily reports), e-commerce domain. Depth is L2: writes tests in an existing framework, hasn't shown building one.
5. CV-030: 11 years of Java. Built a reusable Selenium framework adopted by 6 projects, with a 2,000-case regression in 2 hours on Jenkins. English and Japanese backed by client work (bilingual reports, status calls).

Trade-offs:
- To build or own a framework, look first at CV-039, CV-033 and CV-030. For writing tests in an existing framework, CV-027 fits.
- CV-042, CV-003 and CV-002 are ranked 6–8 as 'possible' fits. I haven't reviewed them in detail.
- The JD doesn't say whether API, mobile or performance testing is in scope, or whether ISTQB or a domain counts. I ranked on web UI only. Tell me if any of these matter and I'll re-weight and re-rank.
